name: json-schema-validation-p5
prompt: what is a good way to reject malformed request bodies at the edge before they reach my handler logic

chunks.content: added a dark mode toggle that persists the choice in local storage
raised the connection pool cap to 80 after seeing checkout timeouts under load
a nightly cron purges soft-deleted rows older than 90 days
the signup form enforces a minimum password length and rejects entries found in a breached-password list
automated certificate renewal so the gateway swaps in a fresh cert 30 days before expiry
the validator coerces obvious types like numeric strings to numbers but refuses unknown properties so a typo'd field is caught instead of silently ignored
the same request shapes are defined once and shared between the server validator and the generated client types so the contract stays in sync
decided to validate every incoming payload against a declared JSON Schema in middleware and return 422 with the offending field paths before the controller ever runs
set a low TTL on the API record so failover to the secondary region propagates quickly
escape user-supplied HTML in comments so a malformed script payload can't run in another viewer's browser
malformed bodies return a consistent error envelope listing each invalid pointer and the rule it broke, so the frontend can highlight the bad inputs
the ops dashboard charts request volume and error rate per endpoint
moved the receipt email into a templating engine with localized strings
added a kill switch flag to instantly disable the recommendations widget if it misbehaves
record every permission grant in an append-only audit log
